conceptual assets.concept: GPIO output register and driven pin values
conceptual assets.reasoning: The bus write flow stores output configuration into port_out: in bus_access on a write to addr_out_c the RTL executes port_out <= bus_req_i.data(GPIO_NUM-1 downto 0). The output_stage process drives gpio_o(GPIO_NUM-1 downto 0) from port_out. Corrupting the stored port_out or the driven gpio_o would change externally observed pin values and violate the implemented write->drive relation, establishing an integrity property (the register stores the authoritative output and the port is the exit point).

conceptual assets.concept: Sampled GPIO input state and one-cycle history
conceptual assets.reasoning: Inputs are captured on clock edges: input_stage registers port_in <= gpio_i(GPIO_NUM-1 downto 0) and port_in2 <= port_in. The bus read path returns port_in on reads to addr_in_c, and irq_trigger uses port_in and port_in2 to compute triggers. Thus the sampled input values and their one-cycle history are used for readback and interrupt decisions; corruption of these stored samples would produce incorrect read results and incorrect trigger behavior, establishing integrity.

conceptual assets.concept: Per-pin interrupt configuration (type, polarity, enable, clear mask)
conceptual assets.reasoning: Configuration registers are written by the bus: bus_access on write decodes addr_tt_c/addr_tp_c/addr_ie_c/addr_ip_c and assigns irq_typ, irq_pol, irq_en, irq_clrn <= bus_req_i.data(...). These registers are read by logic and used by other flows: irq_trigger reads irq_typ/irq_pol to form the trigger expression, and irq_buffer uses irq_en and irq_clrn in the pending-update equation. Corrupting these stored configuration values changes trigger semantics and pending/clear behavior, establishing integrity for the configuration registers.

For each pin the combinational irq_trigger process computes irq_trig(i) from sel_v := irq_typ(i) & irq_pol(i) and the sampled inputs (examples: when "10" => irq_trig(i) <= (not port_in(i)) and port_in2(i); when "11" => irq_trig(i) <= port_in(i) and (not port_in2(i))). irq_trig is then consumed by irq_buffer to update irq_pend. The computed trigger decision is therefore a security-relevant event whose corruption would incorrectly set or suppress pending interrupts, establishing integrity of the computed decision.

conceptual assets.concept: Interrupt pending flags and the CPU IRQ output
conceptual assets.reasoning: The irq_buffer process stores irq_pend on clock edges with irq_pend <= irq_en and ((irq_pend and irq_clrn) or irq_trig) and drives cpu_irq_o <= or_reduce_f(irq_pend). irq_pend is the stored indicator of active pending interrupts and cpu_irq_o is the output presented to the CPU. Corrupting or preventing irq_pend updates, or corrupting cpu_irq_o, would alter interrupt delivery; this establishes an integrity requirement for irq_pend and the exit-point cpu_irq_o (availability to signal interrupts is also implemented by the clocked update, noted in the update relation).
